subject: math
title: Addition and Subtraction Word Problems within 20
seo_title: Grade 1 Word Problems within 20 Worksheets: Add To, Take From, Put Together, Compare and Missing Numbers
standard_text: Use addition and subtraction within 20 to solve word problems involving situations of adding to, taking from, putting together, taking apart, and comparing, with unknowns in all positions, e.g., by using objects, drawings, and equations with a symbol for the unknown number to represent the problem.
meta_desc: Free Grade 1 word problem worksheets within 20: add to, take from, put together, take apart and compare stories with pictures, missing start or change, and equations with a ☐. 100 practice questions for 1st grade with an answer key.
key_big: Act out the story. Then find the missing number.
key_sub: Are some added, taken away, put together or compared? Draw it, then write an equation with a ☐ where the missing number goes. “How many more” means find the difference.
body_html:
Picture the story

Read the story. Ask: what is happening? Are some added, taken away, put together or compared? Then find the number you do not know. It can be the start, the change or the end.

Five kinds of stories

KindStoryEquation
Add toMia had 5 apples. She picked 3 more. How many now?5 + 3 = ☐
Take fromLeo had 9 balloons. 4 popped. How many are left?9 − 4 = ☐
Put togetherAva has 6 red and 5 blue balls. How many in all?6 + 5 = ☐
Take apartSam has 12 balls. 5 are red. The rest are blue. How many are blue?5 + ☐ = 12
CompareAva has 8 stickers. Leo has 5. How many more does Ava have?5 + ☐ = 8

Draw it

When some are added, draw them. Then count them all.

When some are taken away, draw them all. Cross out the ones that go away.

A part-part-whole mat shows two parts and the whole. If you know both parts, add. If you know the whole and one part, subtract.

To compare, line up the two rows. Match one to one. The extra ones are the answer.

Use a box for the missing number

Write an equation. Put a ☐ where the missing number goes. The box can be at the start, in the middle or at the end.

Missing change

Mia had 6 stickers. She got some more. Now she has 9. How many did she get?

6 + ☐ = 9. Count on from 6: 7, 8, 9. That is 3.

Answer: 3 stickers

Missing start

Sam had some shells. He found 4 more. Now he has 11. How many did he have at first?

☐ + 4 = 11. Take away the 4 he found: 11 − 4 = 7.

Answer: 7 shells

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Adding when the story asks “how many more”Line up the two rows. Count the extra ones, or subtract: 8 − 5 = 3.
Adding the two numbers when the start or change is missingWrite the equation with a ☐ first. Check your answer in the story.
Giving the bigger number as the answerThe bigger number is the whole. The answer is the missing part.
Counting one too many or one too fewTouch each picture once. Count on from the bigger number.

faq.q: What kinds of word problems do 1st graders solve?
faq.a: First graders solve add to, take from, put together, take apart and compare stories with numbers up to 20. The missing number can be the start, the change or the end.

faq.q: How can I help my 1st grader with “how many more” problems?
faq.a: Line up two rows of objects and match them one to one. The extra objects are the answer, so 8 − 5 = 3 or 5 + ☐ = 8.

faq.q: What does the box mean in an equation like ☐ + 4 = 11?
faq.a: The box stands for the missing number. Here it is the start, and 11 − 4 = 7, so the box is 7.

faq.q: Should first graders use key words to solve word problems?
faq.a: Not by themselves. Key words like “more” can trick children, so have them act out or draw the story and then decide to add or subtract.

sets.title: Find the missing change or start

items.q: A pet store had 5 fish in a tank. The store got some more fish. Now there are 9 fish in the tank. How many fish did the store get?
items.e: The change is missing: 5 + ☐ = 9. Count on from 5 to 9: 6, 7, 8, 9. That is 4. Answer: 4 fish.

items.q: Leo made a tower with 5 blocks. He took off some blocks. Now the tower has 2 blocks. How many blocks did Leo take off?
items.e: The change is missing: 5 − ☐ = 2. Subtract: 5 − 2 = 3. Check: 5 − 3 = 2. Answer: 3 blocks.

items.q: There were 10 cookies on a plate. The children ate some cookies. Now there are 3 cookies on the plate. How many cookies did the children eat?
items.e: The change is missing: 10 − ☐ = 3. Subtract: 10 − 3 = 7. Check: 10 − 7 = 3. Answer: 7 cookies.

items.q: Omar had 3 balls. He found some more. Now he has 5 balls. How many balls did Omar find?

items.e: We do not know how many were added. Put the ☐ there: 4 + ☐ = 13. The ☐ is 9. Answer: 4 + ☐ = 13.
